'''Steven Kenneth Chapman''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRSE|FRSC|CChem}} (born 1959) is a British chemist and academic. He served as [[Vice-Chancellor]] of [[Edith Cowan University]] in [[Perth]], Western Australia, between 2015 and 2024. Before that, he was Principal and Vice-Chancellor of [[Heriot-Watt University]] in [[Edinburgh]].

==Early life==
Steve Chapman was born on 12 May 1959.{{citation needed|date=October 2024}} Chapman studied at [[Newcastle University]], where he received a First Class [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] (Hons) degree in [[Chemistry]] (1980) and completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Chemistry (1983). Steve Chapman carried out his postdoctoral studies at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] on a NATO Research Fellowship from 1983 to 1985.{{citation needed|date=October 2024}}

==Career==
[[File:FM opens new £35m Heriot-Watt campus in Dubai (6308151171).jpg|Chapman with First Minister of Scotland [[Alex Salmond]] in Dubai, 2011|thumb]]
Chapman returned to the UK in 1985 and was a Lecturer and then Senior Lecturer at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1985 to 1995, and Professor of Biological Chemistry from 1996. In 2000, he became Head of the University's School of Chemistry, and in August 2006, was appointed as Vice-Principal of Planning, Resources and Research Policy at the University.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.ed.ac.uk/news/archive_06.html|title=Congratulations to Professor Steve Chapman|date=2 June 2006|publisher=[[University of Edinburgh]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090905034108/http://www.chem.ed.ac.uk/news/archive_06.html|archive-date=5 September 2009|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Externally, Chapman's roles have included the [[HEFCE]] TRAC(T) Steering Group, the Research and Knowledge Transfer Committee of the [[Scottish Funding Council]], and as a representative on [[LERU]] and [[Universitas 21]]. He was a member of the Board of [[Universities and Colleges Employers Association|UCEA]] and was a previous member of the Board of Directors of Edinburgh Research and Innovation Limited.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.research-innovation.ed.ac.uk/foi/directors.asp|title=Freedom of Information Publication Scheme|accessdate=24 September 2009|publisher=University of Edinburgh}}</ref> He has published over 200 research publications and in 2001 received the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Interdisciplinary Award for major contributions to science at the Chemistry/Biology interface.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/pdf/awards/interdisform.pdf|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate=24 September 2009|title=Royal Society of Chemistry Interdisciplinary Awards 2004}}</ref> In 2005 Chapman became a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the Royal Society of Chemistry.

Chapman was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2016 New Year Honours]] for services to higher education as Vice-Chancellor of Heriot-Watt.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61450|supp=y|page=N8|date=30 December 2015}}</ref>

In April 2015, Chapman commenced his role as Vice-Chancellor and President of [[Edith Cowan University]] in [[Perth]], Western Australia.<ref>{{cite news |title=ECU Vice-Chancellor retirement announced |url=https://www.ecu.edu.au/newsroom/articles/news/ecu-vice-chancellor-retirement-announced |access-date=1 October 2024 |work=ecu.edu.au |date=7 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title='Visionary' ECU leader announces retirement |url=https://thewest.com.au/news/education/edith-cowan-university-vice-chancellor-steve-chapman-to-retire-c-11513751 |access-date=1 October 2024 |work=The West Australian |date=7 August 2023 |language=en}}</ref> After 17 years as a Vice-Chancellor in the United Kingdom and Australia, he retired on 31 July 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=A visionary leader and Vice-Chancellor says farewell to ECU |url=https://www.ecu.edu.au/newsroom/articles/news/a-visionary-leader-and-vice-chancellor-says-farewell-to-ecu |access-date=1 October 2024 |work=ecu.edu.au |date=31 July 2024}}</ref>
